another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now, regarding Alex:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards looking after him (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. I do help out with some money for his clothes and things, but it's not a huge amount - I give about £10 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful to know.

The current Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child is £25.60 per week. To remain eligible for Child Benefit when a child lives with someone else, you would generally need to contribute at least that amount (or the equivalent in kind) towards Alex's upkeep.

Since you mentioned you contribute around £10 per week, this is below the Child Benefit threshold.

A couple more questions to clarify the situation:

1. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, the person he lives with)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum claims it - Alex lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's why:

1. **Alex doesn't live with you** – When a child lives with someone else, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep. The current rate is £25.60 per week, and you mentioned you contribute around £10 per week, which is below this threshold.

2. **Only one person can claim** – Alex's mother is already claiming Child Benefit for him. Since only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child, and she lives with Alex and is already the claimant, she has priority.

**What you could consider:**

If your circumstances change in the future – for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week and his mother agrees to stop her claim – you may then become eligible to claim.

If you have any other questions or if your situation changes, please don't hesitate to ask. I'm happy to help!
